title: Middle Powers at a Crossroads: Malaysia-Mexico Mobility-Centered Collaboration Amidst Rising U.S.-China Tensions
gist: An ASPI-published essay argues Malaysia should pursue its regional innovation hub goal through a mobility-centered middle-power partnership with Mexico (scientific exchanges, technology sharing, a bilateral talent corridor), since intra-ASEAN options are limited and US-China tensions disrupt value chains.

insights.claim: Malaysia is pursuing a regional innovation hub strategy, with MRANTI applying 5G and AI to reduce agricultural losses and optimize soil conditions using climate data, while navigating geopolitical tensions and trade wars.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Malaysia is positioning in applied AI/agtech and not just investment incentives.
insights.locator: Walking around the Malaysian Research Accelerator

insights.claim: Investment and industrial policy alone will not make Malaysia a regional innovation hub; it also needs partnerships that circulate technology, innovation and talent.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Talent and tech-access constraints may cap Malaysia's upside despite FDI inflows.
insights.quote: However, investment and industrial policy alone are not the answer.

insights.claim: Intra-ASEAN mobility-centered collaboration is limited by stagnating intra-ASEAN trade, uneven tech and advanced manufacturing maturity across members, and fragmentation worsened by South China Sea tensions and tariffs on the bloc.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: ASEAN members are pursuing individual de-risking strategies, which weakens bloc-level integration as a thesis.
insights.locator: While Malaysia could opt to try this mobility-centered collaboration

insights.claim: Malaysia and Mexico are usually seen as rivals for FDI and as China+1 alternatives for US and European firms, and Malaysians are unhappy about Mexico's tariffs and moves to cut imports from Asia.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: The competition for China+1 investment is real and complicates any bilateral cooperation.
insights.locator: Upon first glance, Mexico may not seem like the obvious choice

insights.claim: Both Malaysia and Mexico belong to CPTPP and APEC, and Mexico adds a skilled talent pool and complementary industrial and scientific capabilities, making a renewed bilateral relationship feasible.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: CPTPP is the existing treaty channel through which such cooperation could be built.
insights.locator: However, a closer examination paints a different picture

insights.claim: Malaysia's semiconductor ecosystem, built on 50 years of experience, complements Mexico's strong automotive and robotics industries, so bilateral technology sharing with national-security safeguards could keep both competitive.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Points to possible semiconductor-automotive supply chain linkages between Southeast Asia and Mexico.

insights.claim: Malaysia and Mexico share concerns over climate change's impact on food security and could collaborate on AgTech and use CPTPP to improve market access for agricultural SMEs.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: AgTech cooperation is an early-stage theme with limited concrete commitments.
insights.locator: Both countries also share concerns over climate change

insights.claim: The proposed pillars are scientific exchanges (joint research in semiconductors, AgTech, AI and renewables plus joint degree programs), technology sharing, and a bilateral talent corridor.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: A template for middle-power cooperation that could be copied by other states.
insights.locator: Three pillars of a strengthened Malaysia-Mexico partnership

insights.claim: Malaysia faces a talent shortage, and a first-of-its-kind reciprocal circular migration scheme for high-skilled workers such as engineers, scientists and AI researchers could ease it by extending CPTPP's temporary movement provisions to longer stays with visa, tax and relocation incentives.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: High-skilled labor shortages are a binding constraint on Malaysia's tech sector growth.
insights.quote: Malaysia is struggling with finding talent.

insights.claim: Rising protectionism and border closures can be turned into an opportunity for middle powers willing to go against the grain by collaborating on the circulation of innovation, technology and talent.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Mobility-based cooperation is a hedge against US-China rivalry rather than a bet on either side.
insights.quote: While countries are turning to protectionist policies and closing their borders, that “risk” can be turned on its head
insights.locator: While countries are turning to protectionist policies
